correctness.rationale: Computed f=AB^r with A=u^q-u and B=1+A^(q-1), f’=-B^(r-1), hence Gauss [1:(u^(q²)-u)/z:-u^(q²)]. The auxiliary w=c^(-1/q)z^(q^(n-1))/B^((r-1)/q) satisfies (u^(q²)-u)/z=w^q and dw/w=-t B’/B du nonzero; because K=k(u^q,w) the Gauss image field k(u^(q²),w^q)=K^q, giving exact inseparability degree q. Pole order Nq² in this base-point-free Gauss linear series gives dual degree Nq. At finite z=0, f’ vanishes only at q²-q roots of B and gcd(N,r)=1 gives unibranch cusps; infinity is smooth. Independently checked derivative/congruence/genus for q=3,4,n=4; finite checks do not certify the general claim.
